stem:
Fabrikam, Inc. reviews the Microsoft Copilot readiness report in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The report shows that 400 users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses are not counted under **Users on an eligible update channel**. The change advisory board requires that their devices receive new Microsoft 365 Apps features once a month on a predictable release date.

Which update channel should you assign to the devices of these users?
choices: Monthly Enterprise Channel
Beta Channel
Current Channel (Preview)
Current Channel
explanation: The readiness report counts a user as being on an eligible update channel when their devices are on Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel. Of the two eligible channels, only Monthly Enterprise Channel releases feature updates on a fixed date, the second Tuesday of each month.
rationale: Correct: Monthly Enterprise Channel is counted as an eligible update channel in the readiness report, and it releases one update per month on the second Tuesday, which meets the predictable schedule required by the change advisory board.

Incorrect: Beta Channel gives the earliest unsupported builds to Microsoft 365 Insiders for testing. It is not counted as eligible and is not suited to production users. Use it only on test devices that evaluate future features.

Incorrect: Current Channel (Preview) is a preview channel for validating upcoming Current Channel builds on a small set of devices. It is not counted as an eligible channel in the readiness report and has no fixed monthly date. Use it for a small pilot ring.

Incorrect: Current Channel is an eligible channel for Copilot, but it delivers features as soon as they are ready with no set schedule, so it fails the predictable release date requirement. Use it when users must get new Copilot features as early as possible.

stem:
Tailspin Toys is preparing a Copilot pilot. A help desk engineer reports that User1 cannot use licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot features. You need to check right away whether the user account of User1 meets the applicable Copilot licensing requirements. Data that can be up to 72 hours old is not acceptable.

Which tool should you use?
choices: the Microsoft Copilot readiness report
the Microsoft 365 connectivity test for the Copilot app
the Copilot License Details diagnostic
the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights
explanation: Microsoft provides the Copilot License Details diagnostic to validate whether a single user account meets the licensing requirements for Copilot features. Reports in the admin center are aggregated and can lag up to 72 hours, and the connectivity tests check the network, not licensing.
rationale: Incorrect: the readiness report shows license eligibility and assignment per user, but it becomes available within 72 hours and its data can have up to 72 hours of latency, which the stem rules out. Use it to plan which users to license.

Incorrect: the connectivity test for the Copilot app checks whether the device can reach the *.cloud.microsoft endpoints. It says nothing about licenses. Use it when users report that the Copilot app cannot connect.

Correct: the Copilot License Details diagnostic checks one user account against the applicable Copilot licensing requirements when you run it, so it gives a current answer for User1 without waiting for report data.

Incorrect: the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights shows readiness, adoption, and impact trends for leaders. It is an aggregated analytics view, not a per-user license check. Use it to report Copilot adoption to IT leaders.

stem:
Contoso, Ltd. users report that Copilot works in the Word, Excel, and PowerPoint desktop apps but does not work in Word for the web, Excel for the web, and PowerPoint for the web. The devices use Microsoft Edge, and an organization-managed browser policy blocks all third-party cookies. The users can open Copilot Chat in the Copilot app.

What should you do to resolve the issue?
choices: Set the policy for optional connected experiences in Office to Enabled.
Add *.cloud.microsoft to the allow list on the proxy and firewall.
Allow third-party cookies for the Office web apps in the browser policy.
Add [*.]safelinks.protection.outlook.com to the CookiesAllowedForUrls policy only.
explanation: Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for the web requires third-party cookies to be enabled in the browser. Because the desktop apps and the Copilot app work, the network path is fine and the browser cookie policy is the cause.
rationale: Incorrect: optional connected experiences affect the availability of some Copilot features in Microsoft 365 Apps, but the stem points to a browser cookie block that only affects the web apps. Change this policy when desktop Copilot features are missing because of privacy controls.

Incorrect: *.cloud.microsoft must be allowed for Copilot, but the Copilot app and the desktop apps already connect, so the network is not blocking Copilot here. Use this step when the Copilot app or all Copilot experiences fail to connect.

Correct: Learn states that third-party cookies must be enabled for Copilot to work in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for the web. Changing the managed browser policy fixes the web apps without affecting the desktop apps that already work.

Incorrect: allowing cookies only for [*.]safelinks.protection.outlook.com fixes the Unable to verify link message when users open links in Copilot Chat responses. It does not allow the cookies that the Office web apps need. Use it when only links in responses fail.

stem:
Northwind Traders uses Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on Monthly Enterprise Channel. Users have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses. On 200 devices, core Copilot features are missing in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote. A device hardening script that ran on those devices disabled several scheduled tasks, including the Office Feature Updates task.

What should you do first?
choices: Remove and reassign the Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses for the users.
Reinstall Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise by using the Office Deployment Tool.
Move the devices to Current Channel by using a Cloud Update profile.
Re-enable the Office Feature Updates task so that it runs on its regular schedule.
explanation: Learn lists the Office Feature Updates task as a requirement: it must run on its regular schedule and reach the required network resources for core Copilot experiences in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote. The update channel and licenses are already correct in this scenario.
rationale: Incorrect: the users already have Copilot licenses, and the issue only affects the devices where the task is disabled. Reassigning licenses does not change device configuration. Do this when a license assignment failed or is missing.

Incorrect: reinstalling with the Office Deployment Tool is disruptive, and the hardening script could disable the task again. The stem already identifies the disabled task as the cause. Use a reinstall when the installation itself is damaged.

Incorrect: Cloud Update can move devices to Current Channel, but Monthly Enterprise Channel is already an eligible channel for Copilot, so changing channels does not address the disabled task. Use it when devices are on a channel that is not eligible.

Correct: the Office Feature Updates task must run on its regular schedule for core Copilot experiences in the desktop apps. The hardening script disabled it, so re-enabling the task restores the missing features without reinstalling anything.

stem:
Wide World Importers is rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot. Copilot integrations fail intermittently in Microsoft 365 Apps. The network team allows a list of individual FQDNs on the proxy, performs Transport Layer Security (TLS) inspection on all traffic, and closes idle connections after 30 seconds.

You need to ensure that Copilot traffic is not blocked or altered.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
choices: Allow only copilot.cloud.microsoft and m365.cloud.microsoft and block other *.cloud.microsoft subdomains.
Block copilot.cloud.microsoft and allow users to reach Copilot Chat from Microsoft Teams only.
Enable TLS inspection for *.cloud.microsoft so that the proxy logs every Copilot prompt.
Ensure full WebSocket Secure (WSS) connectivity to *.office.com, *.cloud.microsoft, and copilot.cloud.microsoft without interference from TLS inspection or short timeouts.
Allow the entire *.cloud.microsoft domain on the proxy and firewall.
explanation: Copilot requires the whole *.cloud.microsoft domain to be allowed, because Microsoft does not support allowing only selected application URLs in that domain. Copilot integrations also need full WSS connectivity; TLS inspection that interferes with the connection and aggressive proxy timeouts make them fail.
rationale: Incorrect: allowing only selected subdomains is exactly the partial allow list that Microsoft does not support for *.cloud.microsoft. It would keep the intermittent failures. A narrow list is only acceptable where Microsoft publishes a fixed FQDN list, which it does not for Copilot.

Incorrect: blocking copilot.cloud.microsoft breaks the Copilot app. If the goal is to stop personal Microsoft account sign-in, Learn recommends tenant restrictions v2 as the targeted control instead. Use tenant restrictions when consumer accounts must be blocked.

Incorrect: TLS inspection is one of the causes of failing WSS connections, so adding more inspection makes the problem worse. Copilot prompts are already auditable in Microsoft Purview Audit and DSPM for AI. Use those tools when prompts must be logged.

Correct: Copilot integrations can fail when the perimeter blocks WSS, when TLS inspection interferes with the connection, or when a proxy enforces aggressive timeouts. Allowing full WSS connectivity to these domains removes all three causes named in the stem.

Correct: Learn tells you to add *.cloud.microsoft to allow lists and states that allowing only selected Microsoft 365 application URLs in the domain is not supported. This replaces the FQDN-by-FQDN list that the proxy uses today.

stem:
Lucerne Publishing is preparing a Microsoft 365 Copilot pilot for 60 users. The Microsoft Copilot readiness report shows that their devices are not on an eligible update channel. IT deployed Microsoft 365 Apps to the devices with the Office Deployment Tool, and the devices appear in Inventory in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. The pilot users must get new Copilot features in Microsoft 365 Apps as soon as they are ready, and the devices of other users must keep their current update channel. You will use cloud update.

Which four actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: Create a Microsoft Entra security group, and add the 60 pilot users.
In the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, expand Cloud Update, and select the profile for Current Channel.
On the profile page, select the Settings tab, and then select Device selection criteria.
Select + Add groups, select the pilot group, and then select Save.
Select + Add channels, and add the Monthly Enterprise Channel built-in group.
In the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, expand Cloud Update, and select the profile for Monthly Enterprise Channel.
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, set Microsoft 365 installation options to Current Channel, and select Save.
explanation: Copilot in Microsoft 365 Apps needs an eligible update channel such as Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel. With cloud update you do not create channel-change jobs: you assign Microsoft Entra groups or built-in channel groups to the profile of the target channel, and cloud update changes the target channel of eligible devices. Cloud update takes precedence over the Office Deployment Tool, while the installation options in the Microsoft 365 admin center affect only installations that users start themselves.
rationale: Step 1: cloud update profiles are assigned to Microsoft Entra groups, so the group with the pilot users must exist before you can select it. A group limits the change to the pilot, and cloud update evaluates its membership at least once a day.

Step 2: each cloud update profile maps to an update channel. Current Channel delivers new features as soon as they are ready, and assigning devices to its profile changes their target channel to Current Channel.

Step 3: Device selection criteria on the Settings tab define which users or devices the profile manages. You do not create or enable profiles manually; a profile becomes active when a group is assigned to it.

Step 4: + Add groups assigns the pilot group, and Save applies it. Cloud update then moves eligible pilot devices to Current Channel according to the rollout configuration of the profile, and other devices are not affected.

Incorrect: a built-in channel group contains every device in Inventory that is on that channel. Adding it to the Current Channel profile would move all Monthly Enterprise Channel devices, not only the pilot. Use + Add channels to onboard or move all devices of a channel in bulk.

Incorrect: the Monthly Enterprise Channel profile moves devices to Monthly Enterprise Channel, which delivers new features once a month on a predictable date instead of as soon as they are ready. Use it when change control needs a monthly release cadence.

Incorrect: Microsoft 365 installation options set the default channel only for unmanaged installations that users start themselves from Office.com. They do not change devices deployed with the Office Deployment Tool. Use them to choose the channel for self-service installations.

stem:
Proseware, Inc. assigned Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses to 50 users. Copilot works for these users in Teams chats and in Word, but Copilot cannot summarize or draft email in Outlook. The primary mailboxes of the 50 users are hosted on Exchange Server in the on-premises datacenter.

What should you do?
choices: Enable an online archive mailbox for each user in Exchange Online.
Add the users as members of a Microsoft 365 group mailbox.
Migrate the primary mailboxes of the users to Exchange Online.
Grant the users delegate access to a shared mailbox in Exchange Online.
explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot supports primary mailboxes hosted in Exchange Online, and an Exchange Online mailbox is required for experiences that use email, calendar, or meeting data. Copilot can also use archive, shared, and delegate mailboxes that the user can access, but not group mailboxes.
rationale: Incorrect: Copilot can use content in archive mailboxes that the user can access, but the primary mailbox still lives on Exchange Server, so drafting and summarizing the user's own email still fails. An online archive helps when old mail must be searchable.
Incorrect: Microsoft 365 Copilot is not available in group mailboxes, so this adds nothing for Outlook. Group mailboxes are the right tool for shared team conversations, not for Copilot grounding.
Correct: mailbox-grounded Copilot experiences require the primary mailbox to be in Exchange Online. Moving the mailboxes from Exchange Server to Exchange Online removes the blocker for Outlook.

Incorrect: Copilot can use shared and delegate mailboxes that the user is permitted to access, but this does not move the user's own primary mailbox to Exchange Online. Use shared mailboxes when several users must work in one inbox.

stem:
You are evaluating the readiness of Relecloud for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
choices: Office worker devices on Monthly Enterprise Channel are counted under Users on an eligible update channel in the Microsoft Copilot readiness report.
The current proxy configuration meets the Copilot network requirements if copilot.cloud.microsoft is added to the list of allowed FQDNs.
After a Microsoft 365 Copilot license is assigned to a call center user, the user can use Copilot in the desktop apps on the shared call center devices.
explanation: The readiness report counts users on Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel. Copilot needs the full *.cloud.microsoft domain and WSS connectivity without interfering TLS inspection, and it is not available with device-based licensing for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.
rationale: Yes: the readiness report defines Users on an eligible update channel as users enrolled in Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel. Most Relecloud office devices use Monthly Enterprise Channel, so those users are counted.

No: the proxy allows individual FQDNs and performs TLS inspection. Copilot requires the entire *.cloud.microsoft domain, because a partial allow list is not supported, and WSS connections fail when TLS inspection interferes. Adding one FQDN does not fix either problem.

No: Microsoft 365 Copilot is not available with device-based licensing for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise. The call center devices would need user-based activation of Microsoft 365 Apps before Copilot works in the desktop apps.

stem:
Adventure Works Cycles has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and SharePoint Advanced Management. Before the Copilot rollout, you need a baseline that shows which SharePoint and OneDrive sites give access to the largest number of users, including sites that grant access to Everyone except external users.

Which report should you run first in the SharePoint admin center?
choices: the Shared with Everyone except external users activity report
the Sharing links activity report
the Sensitivity label applied to files snapshot report
the Site permissions across your organization snapshot report
explanation: Data access governance reports come in two kinds: snapshot reports show the current permission state across all sites, and activity reports show sharing in the last 28 days. Microsoft recommends starting with the site permissions snapshot report to get the baseline, then using activity reports to track new oversharing.
rationale: Incorrect: this activity report tracks sites where content was shared with all internal users in the last 28 days. It misses broad access granted before that window. Use it to monitor ongoing EEEU sharing after you have the baseline.

Incorrect: the sharing links report is an activity report that lists sites where users created the most sharing links in the last 28 days. It shows recent activity, not the full baseline. Run it monthly after the baseline to catch new oversharing.

Incorrect: this snapshot report finds sites that contain files with a specific sensitivity label. It helps you check protection of labeled content, not the number of users with access. Use it to verify policies on your most sensitive files.

Correct: the site permissions report is a snapshot of the permission structure across all SharePoint and OneDrive sites, and it identifies sites with the broadest access, including Everyone except external users permissions. Learn recommends running it first.

stem:
Contoso Pharmaceuticals uses restricted access control on several SharePoint sites to prepare for Microsoft 365 Copilot. Members of these sites still share files with users who are not in the restricted access control groups, which creates links that lead to access denied errors and shows up in oversharing reports. You need to block sharing of these sites and their content with anyone who is not a member of a control group, including sharing by site owners.

Which command should you run?
choices: `Set-SPOTenant -AllowSharingOutsideRestrictedAccessControlGroups $false`
`Set-SPOSite -Identity $siteUrl -DisableSharingForNonOwners`
`Set-SPOSite -Identity $siteUrl -SharingCapability Disabled`
`Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedAccessControlManagement $true`
explanation: By default, sharing a site that uses restricted access control does not follow the policy: users can still share content with people outside the control groups, who then get access denied. The opt-in tenant setting AllowSharingOutsideRestrictedAccessControlGroups set to $false blocks sharing with users and groups that are not in the control groups, including Everyone except external users and SharePoint groups. Site sharing settings such as SharingCapability control external sharing only.
rationale: Correct: setting AllowSharingOutsideRestrictedAccessControlGroups to $false is the opt-in tenant capability that blocks sharing of restricted sites and their content with users and groups outside the restricted access control groups, for owners and members alike.

Incorrect: DisableSharingForNonOwners stops members from sharing the site, but site owners can still share content with anyone in the organization, so the requirement to block owners too is not met. Use it when only owners should be allowed to share a site.

Incorrect: SharingCapability Disabled turns off external sharing for the site. Internal users who are not in the control groups can still be given links, so the oversharing continues. Use it when a site must not be shared with guests or anonymous users.

Incorrect: DelegateRestrictedAccessControlManagement lets site admins turn restricted access control on or off and change the control groups, with a justification. It does not change sharing behavior. Use it when site owners should manage the policy themselves.

stem:
Fourth Coffee has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and SharePoint Advanced Management. You need to use SharePoint Online Management Shell to find SharePoint sites where any user can access content, download the results, and ask the owner of one overshared site to review its permissions.

Which five actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: `Connect-SPOService -Url https://fourthcoffee-admin.sharepoint.com`
`Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionedUsers -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -CountOfUsersMoreThan 0 -Name "Baseline"`
`Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionedUsers`
`Export-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportID $reportId -DownloadPath "C:\DAGReports"`
`Start-SPOSiteReview -ReportID $reportId -SiteID $siteId -Comment "Check for org wide access"`
`Connect-SPOService -Url https://fourthcoffee-admin.sharepoint.com -Credential $cred`
`Start-SPOAuditDataCollectionForActivityInsights -ReportEntity SharingLinks_Anyone`
`Set-SPOSite -Identity $siteUrl -RestrictedAccessControl $true`
explanation: A data access governance workflow in PowerShell is: connect, start the report, track it until it is Completed to get the report ID, export the CSV, and then start a site access review for a site from that report by using the report ID and site ID from the CSV.
rationale: Step 1: all data access governance cmdlets need a SharePoint Online session. Learn says to connect without the Credential parameter, which is not supported in line with security best practices.
Step 2: the PermissionedUsers snapshot report with CountOfUsersMoreThan 0 lists every site where at least one user can access content. The cmdlet returns a report ID that you track next.

Step 3: Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight shows the status of the report and its report ID. You wait until the status is Completed before you can download it; the first report can take up to five days.
Step 4: Export-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight downloads the completed report as a CSV file. The CSV contains the site IDs that the review command needs.
Step 5: Start-SPOSiteReview uses the report ID and the site ID from the CSV and sends an email to the site owner, which is the collaborative remediation step for an overshared site.
Incorrect: signing in with the Credential parameter is not supported for these cmdlets. Use Connect-SPOService without Credential and complete the interactive or modern authentication sign-in.

Incorrect: you enable audit data collection only for recent activity reports in tenants without SharePoint Advanced Management. Fourth Coffee has SharePoint Advanced Management and runs a snapshot report. Use it in an E5-only tenant before an activity report.

Incorrect: restricted access control limits site access to members of specific groups. It is an immediate remediation that changes access, but the requirement is a review by the site owner. Use it when access must be cut off before any review.

stem:
Coho Winery has Microsoft 365 E5 licenses but no Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and no SharePoint Advanced Management. Before buying Copilot, you need to use PowerShell to find SharePoint sites to which Everyone except external users was added in the last 28 days, and download the results as a CSV file.

Which five actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: `Connect-SPOService -Url https://cohowinery-admin.sharepoint.com`
`Start-SPOAuditDataCollectionForActivityInsights -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite`
Wait 24 hours, and then run `Get-SPOAuditDataCollectionStatusForActivityInsights -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite` until it returns InProgress.
`Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite -Workload SharePoint -ReportType RecentActivity -Name "PublicSiteViaEEEU"`
`Export-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportID $reportId`
`Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionedUsers -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -CountOfUsersMoreThan 0`
`Start-SPOSiteReview -ReportID $reportId -SiteID $siteId -Comment "Remove EEEU"`
explanation: Without SharePoint Advanced Management, an E5 tenant can use data access governance activity reports, but it must first enable audit data collection and wait 24 hours. Snapshot reports and remedial actions such as site access reviews are not available in that case.
rationale: Step 1: the data collection, report, and export cmdlets all run in a SharePoint Online Management Shell session, so you connect first.
Step 2: without SharePoint Advanced Management, you must enable data collection for recent activity based reports. Collection only covers activity from the point it is enabled.
Step 3: reports can be generated 24 hours after collection starts. The status cmdlet returns NotInitiated, InProgress, or Paused, and reports can be generated when it returns InProgress.
Step 4: this RecentActivity report lists SharePoint sites that had Everyone except external users added to site membership in the last 28 days, and it returns the report ID for the export.
Step 5: after the report completes, Export-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight downloads it as a CSV file; the default path is the Downloads folder when DownloadPath is omitted.

Incorrect: E5 tenants without SharePoint Advanced Management cannot generate snapshot reports, and the requirement is about the last 28 days anyway. Use the PermissionedUsers snapshot when the tenant has SharePoint Advanced Management and needs a baseline.

Incorrect: site access reviews are a SharePoint Advanced Management remedial action that is not available to an E5-only tenant, and the requirement ends with downloading the CSV. Use it after Copilot licenses bring SharePoint Advanced Management to the tenant.

stem:
Trey Research has SharePoint Advanced Management and is preparing a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout. A site named Site1 is connected to a Microsoft 365 group named Deals. Over time, many Site1 files were shared directly with users who are not members of Deals. Only members of Deals must be able to open Site1 content, including in Copilot and search results, even when a file was shared with another user. Site access restriction is not yet allowed in the tenant, and only SharePoint administrators may manage it. Afterward, you must download a list of the sites that the policy protects.

Which five actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: `Connect-SPOService -Url https://treyresearch-admin.sharepoint.com`
`Set-SPOTenant -EnableRestrictedAccessControl $true`
`Set-SPOSite -Identity $site1Url -RestrictedAccessControl $true`
`Start-SPORestrictedAccessForSitesInsights -RACProtectedSites`
`Get-SPORestrictedAccessForSitesInsights -RACProtectedSites -ReportId $reportId -Action Download`
`Set-SPOSite -Identity $site1Url -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true`
`Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedAccessControlManagement $true`
`Start-SPORestrictedAccessForSitesInsights -ActionsBlockedByPolicy`
explanation: Restricted access control (site access restriction) limits a site to members of up to 10 control groups. Users outside these groups cannot open the content even with existing permissions or sharing links, and Copilot and search honor the policy. It must be allowed for the tenant before you set it on a site, and for a group-connected site the connected Microsoft 365 group is the default control group. The RACProtectedSites insights report lists protected sites; you generate it and then download it.
rationale: Step 1: Connect-SPOService connects SharePoint Online Management Shell to the admin URL. Every tenant, site, and insights cmdlet that follows needs this session.

Step 2: EnableRestrictedAccessControl allows site-level access restriction for the organization. It must be on before you can configure the policy for an individual site, and it can take up to one hour to take effect.

Step 3: RestrictedAccessControl $true applies the policy to Site1. Because Site1 is group-connected, Deals is the default control group, so users who are not in Deals lose access even through direct sharing, and Copilot no longer shows them the content.

Step 4: Start-SPORestrictedAccessForSitesInsights -RACProtectedSites generates the report of sites protected by the policy. You run it after Site1 is protected so that Site1 is included; the report can take a few hours.
Step 5: the Download action with the report ID saves the protected-sites report to the folder where you run the command, which gives the downloadable list that the stem asks for.

Incorrect: RestrictContentOrgWideSearch turns on Restricted Content Discovery, which hides Site1 from Copilot and organization-wide search but keeps permissions, so users who received a sharing link can still open the files. Use it when access must stay unchanged and only discovery should stop.

Incorrect: DelegateRestrictedAccessControlManagement lets site admins manage the policy with a justification, which breaks the requirement that only SharePoint administrators manage it. Use it when site owners should control access restriction for their own sites.

Incorrect: the ActionsBlockedByPolicy report shows access denials caused by the policy in the past 28 days, such as the top denied users and sites. It does not list protected sites. Use it to see who is blocked after the policy is applied.

stem:
Woodgrove Bank reviews the default data risk assessment in Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) for AI. You must remediate four findings by using the options on the **Protect** tab of the site flyout.

Which option should you use for each finding? To answer, drag the appropriate options to the correct findings. Each option may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
choices: Restrict access by label
Restrict all items
Create an auto-labeling policy
Create retention policies
Restricted access control
Site access review
targets: Finding1: Copilot and agents must not summarize files labeled Highly Confidential, wherever the files are stored.
Finding2: Unlabeled files in Site2 contain credit card numbers and must get a sensitivity label without user action.
Finding3: Site3 contains content that no one has accessed for more than three years.
Finding4: All items in Site4 must stop appearing in Copilot while the owners review the site.
explanation: DSPM for AI runs a weekly default data risk assessment of the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage. Its Protect tab offers four remediations: a DLP policy by label, Restricted Content Discovery for all items, an auto-labeling policy, and a retention policy for stale content.
rationale: Finding1: Restrict access by label creates a DLP policy that prevents Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents from summarizing data that has the selected sensitivity labels, so the control follows the label to any location.

Finding2: an auto-labeling policy from Microsoft Purview Information Protection applies a sensitivity label automatically when sensitive information is found in unlabeled files, so users do not have to act.
Finding3: the retention option creates a Data Lifecycle Management policy that deletes content not accessed for at least three years, which removes stale data that Copilot could otherwise surface.
Finding4: Restrict all items uses SharePoint Restricted Content Discovery to exempt the site from Copilot, which hides every item while the owners review permissions.
notes: Restrict access by label: creates a DLP policy for the Microsoft 365 Copilot location that blocks summarization of items with selected labels. Use it when the risk follows a label, not a site.
Restrict all items: applies Restricted Content Discovery so the site's content does not appear in Copilot and organization-wide search. Use it when a whole site must be hidden during a review.
Create an auto-labeling policy: automatically applies a sensitivity label when sensitive information types are found in unlabeled files. Use it to close labeling gaps at scale.
Create retention policies: deletes content that has not been accessed for at least three years. Use it to reduce obsolete data that adds oversharing risk.

Restricted access control: a SharePoint Advanced Management policy that limits site access to members of specific groups. It is not a Protect tab option in DSPM for AI; use it when only one group may open a site.

Site access review: asks site owners to review and update permissions, started from data access governance reports or the Monitor tab. Use it for collaborative remediation, not for an immediate block.

stem:
Litware, Inc. uses Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI. A site named Projects is used by 30 people and is not among the most used sites in the tenant. You need an assessment of Projects that shows how many items contain sensitive information types and how many items are shared with anyone or with everyone in the organization. The assessment must cover the Projects site specifically.

What should you do?
choices: Wait for the next weekly run of the default data risk assessment.
Run an on-demand classification scan of the Projects site.
Create a custom data risk assessment that includes the Projects site.
Generate a site permissions report from the data access governance reports.
explanation: The default data risk assessment runs weekly but only for the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage. For other sites or specific users, you create a custom data risk assessment; you wait at least 48 hours after it runs to see the results, and you duplicate it to run it again.
rationale: Incorrect: the default assessment covers only the top 100 SharePoint sites based on usage, so a small site such as Projects is not included no matter how long you wait. Rely on it for the most used sites.

Incorrect: an on-demand classification scan finds sensitive information types in items that were not scanned, but it is only one action on the Identify tab and does not produce the oversharing assessment. Use it when an assessment shows unscanned items.

Correct: a custom data risk assessment lets you choose specific sites or users and the data sources to scan, so it covers Projects even though the site is not among the top 100 by usage, and it reports sensitive items and sharing data for that site.

Incorrect: the site permissions report shows how many users can access each site, but it does not count sensitive information types and does not provide the DSPM for AI Protect tab actions. Use it for a tenant-wide permissions baseline.

stem:
You need to meet the technical requirement for the HRRecords site.

What should you configure for HRRecords?
choices: a site access review
Restricted SharePoint Search
Restricted Content Discovery
restricted access control
explanation: Restricted Content Discovery hides a site's content from organization-wide search and Copilot discovery without changing permissions, which suits a temporary review. Restricted access control changes who can access the site, and Restricted SharePoint Search is a retiring tenant-wide allow list.
rationale: Incorrect: a site access review asks the HR site owners to fix permissions, which is useful, but it does not stop content from appearing in Copilot while the review runs. Combine it with Restricted Content Discovery for collaborative cleanup.

Incorrect: Restricted SharePoint Search applies a tenant-wide allow list of up to 100 sites, which would affect all 2,300 sites, and it is retiring with new enablement blocked since July 31, 2026. Use Restricted Content Discovery for selected sites instead.

Correct: Restricted Content Discovery stops HRRecords content from appearing in Copilot responses and organization-wide search while permissions stay unchanged. Relecloud has SharePoint Advanced Management through its Copilot licenses, so the feature is available.

Incorrect: restricted access control limits site access to members of specific groups, which changes effective permissions during the review and breaks the requirement. Use it when only one group, such as HR, may open a site at all.

stem:
Alpine Ski House must turn off web search in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat for a security group named Group1. Other users must keep web search.

Which service should you use to configure the **Allow web search in Copilot** policy?
choices: Copilot > Settings > Data access in the Microsoft 365 admin center
the Cloud Policy service in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center
Microsoft Edge configuration policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center
a meeting policy in the Teams admin center
explanation: The Allow web search in Copilot policy is available only in the Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365, and it can target users or groups. The web search entry in Copilot settings only links to that policy service.
rationale: Incorrect: the web search entry under Copilot settings is a link that sends you to create the cloud policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. You do not configure the policy there. Use Copilot settings for controls such as image generation.

Correct: Learn states that the Allow web search in Copilot policy is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365, and a cloud policy can be scoped to Group1 while other users keep the default.

Incorrect: Edge configuration policies manage Copilot Chat behavior in the Edge sidebar, such as whether it can use page content. They do not turn off web search in Copilot. Use them to control browsing context in Edge.
Incorrect: Teams meeting policies control Copilot in meetings, such as whether transcription is required. They do not control web search. Use them for meeting and call experiences.

stem:
Bellows College wants web search to be available by default in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat for staff. Each staff member must be able to stop web content from being used in their own responses.

Which configuration should you use?
choices: Set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled, and let users turn on web search.
Set the Allow web search in Copilot policy to Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat, and let users turn on the Web content toggle.
Leave the Allow web search in Copilot policy not configured, and turn off optional connected experiences for each user.
Set the Allow web search in Copilot policy to Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat, and let users turn off the Web content toggle.
explanation: When admins enable web search, the user-level Web content toggle is on by default and each user can turn it off. When admins disable web search, the toggle is dimmed and users cannot turn it on.
rationale: Incorrect: disabling optional connected experiences turns off web search, but it also restricts Copilot Chat, Copilot, and many other Microsoft 365 experiences, and users cannot override it. Use it only when the organization must block all optional connected experiences.
Incorrect: when the policy disables web search, the Web content toggle is turned off and dimmed, so users cannot turn it on. Use this option when web search must be blocked for a group.

Incorrect: if the policy is not configured, web search is available, but the user privacy setting for optional connected experiences has no effect on web search. Users would still use the Web content toggle, so the per-user change does nothing here.

Correct: with web search enabled, the Web content toggle is on by default, and users can turn it off in Settings > Personalization in the Copilot app. Their preference persists across sessions and devices, which meets both requirements.

stem:
City Power & Light never configured the **Allow web search in Copilot** policy. Users report that Copilot Chat cannot use web search, and that several other Microsoft 365 experiences that use cloud services are also unavailable. Users did not change any personal settings.

Which setting should you identify as the most likely cause?
choices: The Pin Copilot Chat setting is set to Do not pin Copilot Chat in Microsoft 365 apps.
The EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext policy is set to block page context.
The Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy is set to Disabled.
The user privacy setting for optional connected experiences is turned off in Word.
explanation: If the Allow web search in Copilot policy is not configured, web search is available unless the admin sets Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office to Disabled. That policy also restricts Copilot Chat, Copilot, and other experiences, which matches the extra symptoms.
rationale: Incorrect: the pinning setting only controls whether Copilot Chat is pinned in the navigation of Microsoft 365 apps. It does not affect web search. Use it to manage where Copilot Chat appears.

Incorrect: EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext stops Copilot Chat in Edge from using web page or PDF content in responses. It does not turn off web search or other Microsoft 365 experiences. Use it to block browsing context in the Edge sidebar.

Correct: with the web search policy not configured, the admin policy for optional connected experiences decides availability. Setting it to Disabled removes web search and restricts other cloud-backed Microsoft 365 experiences, matching both symptoms.

Incorrect: Learn states that the user privacy setting for optional connected experiences in Microsoft 365 apps has no effect on web search. Web search can still be available when a user turns it off. Users also did not change settings.

stem:

The Allow web search in Copilot policy is not configured, and the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy is set to Enabled. Users report that Copilot Chat never uses web content. The compliance team approved web search for all users.

What should you do?

Set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Not configured.
Create a cloud policy that sets Allow web search in Copilot to Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.
Turn on web search in Copilot > Settings > Data access in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
explanation: In GCC and DoD, web search is available but turned off by default. To enable it, you must configure the Allow web search in Copilot policy in Cloud Policy service; if it is not configured, web search stays off regardless of the optional connected experiences policy.
rationale: Incorrect: the Web content toggle is only available to users when the admin enables web search. In this GCC tenant the policy is not configured, so web search stays off and users cannot turn it on. Users use the toggle to opt out after admins enable it.

Incorrect: in GCC, web search stays off when the web search policy is not configured, regardless of how the optional connected experiences policy is set. In a commercial tenant, Disabled on this policy turns web search off.

Correct: GCC tenants have web search off by default, and the only way to turn it on is to configure the Allow web search in Copilot policy in Cloud Policy service. Setting it to Enabled meets the approved requirement for all users.

Incorrect: the web search entry in Copilot settings only links to the Cloud Policy service. There is no separate toggle there that overrides the cloud policy. Use Copilot settings for controls that live in the admin center, such as image generation.

stem:
Humongous Insurance uses Microsoft 365 Copilot. The **Allow web search in Copilot** policy is not configured. The risk team requires that Researcher, Cowork, and Copilot Work mode never send queries to the web. Copilot Chat must keep web search, and other Microsoft 365 experiences must not be affected. Users must not be able to override the setting.

Solution: You create a cloud policy for all users that sets Allow web search in Copilot to Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat.

Does this meet the goal?
choices: Yes
No
explanation: The third value of the Allow web search in Copilot policy turns off web search in Work mode and, as Learn notes, also in Researcher and Cowork, while Copilot Chat and Web mode keep it. Because it is an admin policy, users cannot turn it back on.
rationale: Correct: Learn states that this option disables web search in Researcher and Cowork, and it disables web search in Work mode while Web mode and Copilot Chat keep it. It changes nothing outside Copilot, and users cannot override an admin-disabled setting.
Incorrect: the solution does meet the goal. No would be right if the policy were set to Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat, because then Copilot Chat would also lose web search.

You need to configure web search to meet the business requirements of Relecloud. You plan to use one policy setting with two scoped configurations.

How should you complete the configuration? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

```text
Service:                    [[1]]
Policy:                     Allow web search in Copilot
Scope LegalGroup:           [[2]]
Scope all other users:      [[3]]
```

targets.label: Box 1
options: Cloud Policy service in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center
Copilot > Settings > Data access in the Microsoft 365 admin center
why: Correct: the Allow web search in Copilot policy is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365, where each configuration can be scoped to a group such as LegalGroup.

Incorrect: the web search entry in Copilot settings only links to the Cloud Policy service, so you cannot scope the setting there. Use Copilot settings for admin center controls such as Copilot image generation.

Incorrect: Edge configuration policies control Copilot Chat in the Edge sidebar, for example whether it can read page content. They do not control web search in Copilot. Use them for browser-specific Copilot behavior.

targets.label: Box 2
options: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
why: Correct: the legal department must not use web search in any Copilot experience, so both Copilot and Copilot Chat must be disabled. The Web content toggle is dimmed and users cannot turn it on.
Incorrect: this value keeps web search in Copilot Chat and Web mode, so legal users could still send queries to the web. Use it for users who may use web search only in chat.

options: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat
Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
why: Incorrect: this value removes web search from Copilot Chat too, which breaks the requirement that Copilot Chat keeps web search for other users. Use it for groups such as LegalGroup that must have no web search.

Correct: this value keeps web search in Copilot Chat and Web mode, and Learn states that it disables web search in Work mode, Researcher, and Cowork, which matches the requirement for all other users.
Incorrect: this value leaves web search on in Researcher, Cowork, and Work mode, which the business requirements forbid for other users. Use it when every Copilot experience may use the web.

explanation: Web search for Copilot and Copilot Chat is managed by one cloud policy with three values: enabled in both, disabled in both, or disabled in Work mode with Web mode and Chat enabled. The third value also disables web search in Researcher and Cowork. Scoped configurations let different groups get different values.

stem:
Margie's Travel has Microsoft 365 E3 licenses for all users and Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses for 200 users. User2 has only a Microsoft 365 E3 license. When User2 selects the **Search** module in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, User2 gets keyword-based results instead of the AI-powered Copilot Search experience.

What should you do so that User2 gets Copilot Search?
choices: Turn on Copilot Search in Copilot > Search in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Assign a Microsoft 365 Copilot license to User2.
Add a search vertical for User2 in Microsoft Search.
Pin Copilot Chat in Microsoft 365 apps for User2.
explanation: Copilot Search needs no setup by an admin, but it requires an eligible Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Users without the license get the Microsoft Search experience when they select the Search module.
rationale: Incorrect: no admin action is needed to set up Copilot Search, and there is no switch that grants it to unlicensed users. The Copilot > Search page is for bookmarks, acronyms, connectors, and analytics.
Correct: users with an eligible Copilot license get Copilot Search from the Search module automatically. User2 has no Copilot license, so User2 receives Microsoft Search until a license is assigned.

Incorrect: verticals customize the Microsoft Search results page, for example to show connector content. They do not turn Microsoft Search into Copilot Search. Use them when unlicensed users must see a custom set of results.

Incorrect: pinning controls whether Copilot Chat appears in the navigation of Microsoft 365 apps. It does not change which search experience the Search module shows. Use it to improve discoverability of Copilot Chat.

stem:
Wingtip Toys curated 150 bookmarks and 80 acronyms in Microsoft Search last year. The company now has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses. You need the same bookmarks and acronyms to appear in Copilot Search with the least administrative effort.

What should you do?
choices: Take no further action, because curated bookmarks and acronyms already apply to Copilot Search.
Re-create the bookmarks and acronyms in Draft state and then publish them.
Create a Copilot connector that indexes the bookmark and acronym lists.
Export the bookmarks and acronyms as CSV files and import them on the Copilot > Search page.
explanation: Copilot Search uses the same curated answers as Microsoft Search. If bookmarks and acronyms are already configured for Microsoft Search, no further action is required for them to work in Copilot Search.
rationale: Correct: Learn states that if you already configured bookmarks and acronyms for Microsoft Search, no further action is required to enable curated bookmarks and acronyms for Copilot Search, which is the least effort.
Incorrect: re-creating answers duplicates work and risks duplicate URL errors. Draft state is useful when a new answer must be reviewed before users can see it, not for answers that already exist.

Incorrect: Copilot connectors index content from external systems into Microsoft Graph. Bookmarks and acronyms are search answers that admins curate, not content to index. Use a connector for data such as tickets or knowledge articles.

Incorrect: CSV import is useful to add or update answers in bulk, but the existing answers already apply, and re-importing URLs that are used in existing bookmarks causes duplicate errors. Use import for a new batch of answers.

stem:
Nod Publishers wants to add the acronym ECO to Copilot Search. The legal team must approve the definition before users can see it in search results.

Which state should you use when you add the acronym?
choices: Excluded
Draft
Scheduled
Published
explanation: Acronyms in Copilot Search have three states: Published (visible), Draft (saved but not shown in results), and Excluded (prevented from appearing). Scheduled is a bookmark state, not an acronym state.
rationale: Incorrect: Excluded prevents an acronym from appearing in search results. It is meant for acronyms that must never be shown, not for a pending review. Use it to suppress a confusing or unwanted acronym.
Correct: acronyms in Draft state do not appear in search results, so the legal team can review ECO first. You then move the acronym to Published to make it visible.

Incorrect: Scheduled is a state for bookmarks, which can publish at a set date and time. Acronyms support only Published, Draft, and Excluded. Use Scheduled for a bookmark that must appear on a launch date.
Incorrect: Published makes the acronym available to users in Copilot Search right away, before legal approval. Use it when the definition is already approved.

stem:
Southridge Video manages 300 bookmarks for Copilot Search. You exported the bookmarks, added new keywords to 40 existing rows, and imported the CSV file. The import fails with errors that the URLs are already used in existing bookmarks.

What should you do before you import the file again?
choices: Clear the URL column of the 40 rows.
Change the State column of the 40 rows to Draft.
Populate the ID column with the bookmark ID of each existing bookmark.
Remove the header row and the empty ID, Last Modified, and Last Modified By columns.
explanation: Copilot Search rejects a bookmark whose URL is already used by another answer. To update existing bookmarks by import, you include the bookmark ID; the row is then treated as an update instead of a new bookmark.
rationale: Incorrect: the URL is required for Published, Suggested, Scheduled, and Draft bookmarks, so clearing it creates new errors. Only Excluded bookmarks need just the URL.

Incorrect: changing the state does not change whether the row is treated as new, so the duplicate URL errors remain, and Draft would also hide the bookmarks. Use Draft for bookmarks that need review before publishing.
Correct: when the bookmark ID is present, the row is not treated as a new addition, so the duplicate URL rule is not triggered and the new keywords update the existing bookmarks.
Incorrect: the file must keep the header row and all columns in the template order. The ID, Last Modified, and Last Modified By columns are the only ones that can be empty, not columns to delete.

stem:
Fabrikam Residences has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses for all users. Users want one experience that answers questions by combining internal documents from Microsoft Graph, ServiceNow content from a Copilot connector, and current public information from the web.

Which experience should you recommend?
choices: Microsoft Copilot Chat
the Microsoft Copilot extension for the browser
Microsoft Copilot Search
Microsoft Search in SharePoint
explanation: Copilot Search is query-based and uses Microsoft Graph and third-party connectors. Copilot Chat is conversational and can use Microsoft Graph, third-party connectors, and the web, so only Copilot Chat combines all three sources.
rationale: Correct: Copilot Chat uses Microsoft Graph, third-party connectors, and the web as data sources, and it generates deeper answers, which matches the request to combine internal, connector, and public web information.

Incorrect: the Microsoft Copilot extension improves Copilot Search results with activity from configured third-party sites such as Jira or ServiceNow. It does not add public web content. Use it to enrich search results from work-related SaaS apps.

Incorrect: Copilot Search searches Microsoft Graph and third-party connectors to find content quickly, but it does not include web results. Recommend it when users need to find a file, ticket, or person fast.
Incorrect: Microsoft Search in SharePoint is keyword-based, has no Copilot integration, and does not use the web. It is the free experience for users without a Copilot license.

stem:
Graphic Design Institute enabled a Copilot connector for its ServiceNow knowledge base. Staff with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses see ServiceNow articles in Copilot Search right away. Staff without Copilot licenses use Microsoft Search and do not see any ServiceNow articles. The college will not buy more Copilot licenses.

What should you do so that unlicensed staff can find the articles?
choices: Configure a search vertical and a result type for the connection in Microsoft Search.
Run a full crawl of the ServiceNow connection.
Change the connector access permissions to Everyone in the organization.
Add the ServiceNow article URLs as bookmarks in Copilot Search.
explanation: Copilot Search supports all tenant-enabled connectors right away with semantic search. Microsoft Search requires admin setup before connector content appears, as verticals with result types and filters, and it has no semantic search.
rationale: Correct: in Microsoft Search, connector content appears only after an admin sets up verticals with result types and filters. Configuring them makes the ServiceNow articles visible to unlicensed staff without buying licenses.

Incorrect: a full crawl refreshes the index, deleted items, and permissions, but the articles are already indexed because Copilot Search shows them. Run a full crawl when permission changes or deletions are not reflected.

Incorrect: access permissions control which users may see indexed items, but licensed staff already see the articles, so permissions are not the gap. Microsoft Search still has no vertical to display them. Change permissions when content is public to all employees.

Incorrect: bookmarks promote individual key resources for specific keywords. Adding every article as a bookmark does not scale and does not make the connector content searchable. Use bookmarks for a small set of important sites and tools.

stem:
Consolidated Messenger manages acronyms and bookmarks on the Copilot > Search page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
choices: A user who searches for kpi does not get the curated answer for the acronym KPI because acronym queries are case sensitive.
When you publish a bookmark, users can discover it right away because the search index refreshes immediately.
When you bulk import acronyms from a CSV file, the State column must contain a value for every row.
explanation: Curated acronyms answer common query forms such as KPI, define KPI, or KPI stands for, regardless of case. Publishing a bookmark refreshes the index immediately, and the acronym CSV import requires the Acronym, Stands For, and State fields.
rationale: No: Learn notes that acronym queries are not case sensitive, so kpi, KPI, and Kpi all return the curated meanings. Case only matters for how you want the acronym displayed.
Yes: when you publish a bookmark in the admin center, the search index refreshes immediately, so users can discover it right away. Use Scheduled when the bookmark should appear later.
Yes: in the acronym import file, Acronym, Stands For, and State are mandatory. State must be Published, Draft, or Excluded for each row.

stem:
Contoso Suites wants to add the acronym ECO to Copilot Search by using Microsoft Graph PowerShell. The legal team must approve the definition in the Microsoft 365 admin center before users can see it.

Which three actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "SearchConfiguration.ReadWrite.All"`
`New-MgSearchAcronym -BodyParameter @{ displayName = "ECO"; standsFor = "Engineering Change Order"; state = "draft" }`
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, open **Copilot** > **Search** > **Acronyms**, review ECO with the legal team, and move it to Published.
`New-MgSearchBookmark -BodyParameter @{ displayName = "ECO"; webUrl = "https://contoso.com/eco"; state = "draft" }`
`Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy"`
`New-MgExternalConnection -BodyParameter @{ id = "eco"; name = "ECO"; description = "Engineering Change Order" }`
explanation: Acronyms are search answers managed through the Microsoft Graph search answers API with the SearchConfiguration permissions. Creating the acronym in draft state keeps it out of results until someone moves it to Published, which fits an approval step.
rationale: Step 1: creating search answers such as acronyms requires the SearchConfiguration.ReadWrite.All permission, so you connect with that scope before you call the API.
Step 2: New-MgSearchAcronym creates the acronym with its display name, meaning, and state draft. Acronyms in Draft state do not appear in Copilot Search results, so users cannot see ECO yet.

Step 3: an acronym in Draft state must be moved to Published to appear in search results, so the final step is the legal review on the Acronyms tab and the move to Published. It needs the draft from step 2.
Incorrect: New-MgSearchBookmark creates a bookmark, which promotes a URL for keywords. It is the wrong answer type for a term definition. Use it to promote key sites and tools in search results.

Incorrect: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy lets you create and manage Copilot connector connections. It does not grant access to search answers such as acronyms. Use it when you build a connector by using Microsoft Graph.

Incorrect: New-MgExternalConnection creates a Copilot connector connection for external content. Acronyms are curated answers, not indexed content. Use it as the first step of a custom synced connector.

stem:
Blue Yonder Airlines wants users to be able to start trials of Microsoft 365 Copilot on their own. Users must not be able to buy Copilot licenses by themselves.

Which option should you select in **Microsoft Copilot self-service purchases**?
choices: Copilot pay-as-you-go billing
Allow trials or purchases
Prevent self-service purchases
Allow trials only
explanation: The Microsoft Copilot self-service purchases setting in Copilot > Settings > User access has three choices: allow trials or purchases, allow trials only, or prevent self-service purchases.
rationale: Incorrect: Copilot pay-as-you-go billing is a separate setting that sets up a billing policy for eligible Copilot Chat usage. It is not an option of the self-service purchases setting. Use it to bill agent usage in Copilot Chat.
Incorrect: this option lets users both start trials and buy Copilot themselves, which breaks the requirement that users must not purchase. Use it when the organization accepts self-service purchases.
Incorrect: this option blocks trials as well as purchases, so users could not start trials. Use it when all Copilot acquisitions must go through IT.
Correct: Allow trials only lets users start a trial of Copilot by themselves while blocking self-service purchases, which matches both requirements.

stem:
Lamna Healthcare Company must turn on the Copilot AI disclaimer for all users. You must follow the principle of least privilege. An auditor who has the Global Reader role must be able to confirm the configuration afterward.

Which role should you assign to the administrator who turns on the disclaimer?
choices: Global Administrator
Global Reader
AI Administrator
Office Apps Administrator
explanation: Turning on the Copilot AI disclaimer requires the AI Administrator role. Global Reader can view Copilot settings but not change them, and Global Administrator is broader than needed.
rationale: Incorrect: Global Administrator can turn on the disclaimer, but it is far broader than needed and breaks least privilege. Reserve it for emergency scenarios.
Incorrect: Global Reader can view but not change Copilot settings, so it fits the auditor, not the administrator who turns on the disclaimer.
Correct: Learn states that you need the AI Administrator role to turn on the Copilot AI disclaimer. It manages Copilot settings without the broad permissions of Global Administrator.

Incorrect: Office Apps Administrator is needed to create Cloud Policy settings for Microsoft 365 apps directly. The disclaimer is turned on from Copilot settings, which creates its cloud policy automatically and requires AI Administrator.

stem:
VanArsdel, Ltd. must make it clear to users of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook that AI-generated content may be inaccurate. The message must be bold, and its tooltip must link to the internal AI use policy page of the company.

Which setting should you configure?
choices: Custom link for blocked Microsoft Copilot app, with the internal policy URL
Custom AI disclaimer on the Workforce Insights landing page
Copilot custom dictionary, with the policy terms added as entries
Copilot AI disclaimer, with the Bold font and a web address for the tooltip
explanation: The Copilot AI disclaimer setting is in Copilot > Settings > View all. It displays a standard or bold message in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, and the Copilot app, and you can add an internal policy URL to the tooltip.
rationale: Incorrect: the custom link for the blocked Copilot app appears only on the Copilot Chat was turned off for your organization page for blocked users. It does not show a disclaimer to active users. Use it to explain why Copilot is blocked.

Incorrect: the Workforce Insights custom AI disclaimer adds a footer to the Workforce Insights agent only. It does not appear in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Outlook. Use it to add guidance for that agent.

Incorrect: the Copilot custom dictionary adds organization-specific vocabulary to supported Teams experiences, such as meeting transcription. It does not display any message. Use it to improve recognition of product names in Teams.

Correct: the Copilot AI disclaimer lets you choose Standard or Bold, and you can enter a web address that is available from the tooltip. The disclaimer appears in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, and the Copilot app.

stem:
Woodgrove Bank wants the whole tenant to receive generally available Microsoft 365 features about 30 days after they reach general availability. A security group named ITValidation must receive generally available features as soon as they are released. Targeted release can no longer be modified in the tenant.

What should you configure in **Copilot Release Preferences: General Availability**?
choices: Select Standard release, and add all other users as exceptions.
Select Standard release, and add ITValidation as an exception.
Select Deferred release, and enroll ITValidation in Copilot Frontier.
Select Deferred release, and add ITValidation as an exception.
explanation: Release preferences have a tenant default of Standard release or Deferred release, plus up to 10,000 user or group exceptions that get the other option. Frontier is a separate opt-in for features before general availability, not for generally available features.
rationale: Incorrect: listing every other user as an exception does not scale and hits the 10,000-exception limit, where each member of a group counts. Choosing Deferred release as the default achieves the same result with one exception.

Incorrect: this makes the tenant Standard release and puts ITValidation on Deferred release, which is the opposite of the requirement. Use it when most users get features at GA and only a few need extra time.

Incorrect: Frontier gives preview features before general availability, which is not the same as Standard release for GA features. ITValidation would still follow Deferred release for features that are not part of Frontier.

Correct: with Deferred release as the default, the tenant receives GA features about 30 days after Standard release starts. Adding ITValidation as an exception assigns that group to Standard release, so it gets GA features as soon as they are released.

stem:
Trey Research wants a security group named EarlyAdopters to receive eligible Copilot agents and features before they reach general availability. All members of EarlyAdopters have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses. Other users must not receive these features.

What should you configure?
choices: Current Channel (Preview) for the devices of EarlyAdopters
Copilot Release Preferences: General Availability, with EarlyAdopters on Standard release
Targeted release for EarlyAdopters in Settings > Org settings
Copilot Frontier, with access set to Specific users and groups
explanation: Frontier is the opt-in program for features before general availability. Standard and Deferred release only decide when generally available features arrive, Targeted release is retiring, and update channels control Microsoft 365 Apps builds, not service features.
rationale: Incorrect: Current Channel (Preview) delivers early Microsoft 365 Apps desktop builds. It does not grant pre-GA Copilot agents or service features. Use it to validate upcoming app builds on a few devices.
Incorrect: Standard release gives features as soon as they are generally available, not before. Use it when a group must not be deferred, as part of the GA release preferences.
Incorrect: Targeted release is retiring in January 2027, and since November 2026 administrators can no longer add or remove users. Microsoft directs customers to Frontier for early access.

Correct: Copilot Frontier offers No access, All users, or Specific users and groups. Selecting EarlyAdopters gives only that group pre-GA features and agents, and its members have the Copilot licenses that Copilot Frontier features need.

stem:
First Up Consultants wants eligible administrators to use the Microsoft 365 Admin agent, the Copilot experience that helps administrators operate Microsoft 365, Copilot, and agents.

Which setting should you configure in **Copilot** > **Settings** > **User access**?
choices: Copilot in Bing, Edge, and Windows
Microsoft Copilot in admin centers
Copilot Frontier
Microsoft Copilot self-service purchases
explanation: Microsoft Copilot in admin centers controls whether eligible admins can use Copilot in supported admin centers. The Microsoft 365 Admin agent is the agentic experience that this setting manages.
rationale: Incorrect: this entry only provides access guidance for Copilot Chat in Bing, Edge, and Windows; it is not a configuration location. Use the linked Edge and Windows guidance for those experiences.
Correct: this User access setting manages whether eligible admins can use Copilot in supported admin centers, which is where the Microsoft 365 Admin agent runs.
Incorrect: Copilot Frontier gives selected users preview features and agents before general availability. It is not the control for Copilot in admin centers. Use it to pilot pre-GA capabilities.
Incorrect: this setting controls whether users can start trials or buy Copilot themselves. It does not affect admin experiences. Use it to govern self-service acquisition.

stem:
Tailspin Toys must stop users from creating AI-generated videos in Microsoft 365 Copilot and supported Microsoft 365 apps. Users must still be able to generate images with Copilot.

What should you do in the Microsoft 365 admin center?
choices: Turn off the Screen and camera sharing setting.
Turn off the Create features in the Copilot app individually.
Turn off the Copilot image generation setting.
Turn off the Copilot video generation setting.
explanation: The Microsoft 365 admin center has separate settings for Copilot image generation and Copilot video generation. Built-in Create features are not configured individually, and Screen and camera sharing controls Vision.
rationale: Incorrect: Screen and camera sharing manages Vision, which lets Copilot see the user's screen or camera. It does not control video generation. Use it to stop users from sharing screens with Copilot.

Incorrect: Learn states that built-in Create features are not configured individually; only brand kits are managed through a cloud policy. Use the dedicated settings for image and video generation instead.

Incorrect: Copilot image generation allows or prevents image-generation experiences. Turning it off breaks the requirement that users can still generate images. Use it when image generation must be blocked.

Correct: the dedicated video generation setting controls whether users can access AI video generation features in Copilot and supported Microsoft 365 apps, so you can block video while images stay available.

stem:
Coho Vineyard has four requirements for Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Which setting should you configure for each requirement? To answer, drag the appropriate settings to the correct requirements. Each setting may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
choices: Microsoft Copilot self-service purchases
Copilot Release Preferences: General Availability
Copilot AI disclaimer
Copilot image generation
Copilot Frontier
Copilot pay-as-you-go billing
targets: Requirement1: Users can start a Copilot trial but cannot buy Copilot themselves.
Requirement2: The tenant receives generally available features about 30 days after Standard release starts.
Requirement3: Supported apps show a bold message that AI-generated content may be inaccurate.
Requirement4: Users cannot create pictures with Copilot.
explanation: Most tenant-wide Copilot controls live in Copilot > Settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center, grouped under User access, Data access, Copilot actions, and Other settings. Learn which setting owns which outcome: acquisition, release timing, transparency, and generation features.
rationale: Requirement1: the self-service purchases setting has an Allow trials only option, which lets users start trials while blocking self-service purchases.
Requirement2: selecting Deferred release in the general availability release preferences delays GA features by about 30 days after the Standard release rollout begins.
Requirement3: the Copilot AI disclaimer displays AI-generated content may be inaccurate in supported apps, and you can choose the Bold font.
Requirement4: Copilot image generation allows or prevents supported image-generation experiences, so turning it off stops users from creating pictures.
notes: Microsoft Copilot self-service purchases: allow trials or purchases, allow trials only, or prevent self-service purchases. Use it to govern how users acquire Copilot.
Copilot Release Preferences: General Availability: choose Standard release or Deferred release for GA features, with up to 10,000 exceptions. Use it to control when GA features arrive.
Copilot AI disclaimer: shows a standard or bold accuracy disclaimer with an optional link to an internal policy. Use it to meet transparency or regulatory requirements.
Copilot image generation: allows or prevents supported image-generation experiences. Use it when image creation must be blocked or allowed.
Copilot Frontier: gives users or groups preview features and agents before general availability. Use it for early evaluation, not for GA timing or blocking features.
Copilot pay-as-you-go billing: sets up a billing policy for eligible Copilot Chat usage through Billing & usage. Use it to pay for agent usage by unlicensed users, not to control purchases.

stem:
Proseware, Inc. wants to pin the Microsoft Copilot app to the Windows taskbar of managed devices by using the taskbar pinning control in **Copilot** > **Settings**. All users have Microsoft Intune licenses. You must follow the principle of least privilege.

Which role should the administrator have?
choices: AI Administrator
Teams Administrator
Intune Administrator
Office Apps Administrator
explanation: The taskbar pinning control in Copilot settings applies only to users with an active Intune license, and viewing or configuring it requires the Intune Administrator role. Other Copilot settings typically use AI Administrator.
rationale: Incorrect: AI Administrator manages most Copilot settings, such as pinning Copilot Chat in Microsoft 365 apps, but Learn states that taskbar pinning requires the Intune Administrator role. Use AI Administrator for Copilot settings that do not touch device management.
Incorrect: Teams Administrator pins the Copilot app inside Teams by using app setup policies in the Teams admin center. It does not pin apps to the Windows taskbar. Use it for the Teams app bar.

Correct: to view or configure Copilot taskbar pinning in the Microsoft 365 admin center, you must be a member of the Intune Administrator role, and the setting applies to users who have an active Intune license.

Incorrect: Office Apps Administrator manages Cloud Policy settings for Microsoft 365 apps, such as the web search policy. It does not control Windows taskbar pinning. Use it for Microsoft 365 Apps policies.

stem:
Fourth Coffee blocks the Copilot app for contractors by using Integrated apps. When contractors open Copilot Chat, they see a page that says Copilot Chat was turned off for the organization. You need that page to link to the internal AI guidance site of the company.

Which setting should you configure?
choices: Copilot AI disclaimer
Copilot diagnostics logs
Pin Microsoft Copilot Chat
Custom link for blocked Microsoft Copilot app
explanation: Users blocked through the Integrated apps control see the Copilot Chat was turned off for your organization page. The Custom link for blocked Microsoft Copilot app setting adds a View info from your organization link to that page.
rationale: Incorrect: the AI disclaimer link appears in a tooltip in supported apps for users who can use Copilot. Blocked contractors never see it. Use it to link active users to an AI policy.

Incorrect: Copilot diagnostics logs let admins submit diagnostic data to Microsoft on behalf of users who cannot submit feedback. They do not change any user-facing page. Use them when you troubleshoot Copilot issues with Microsoft.
Incorrect: pinning controls whether Copilot Chat appears in the navigation of Microsoft 365 apps. It does not add a link to the blocked page. Use it to manage discoverability.
Correct: this setting in Copilot > Settings > View all adds a View info from your organization link that points to your URL on the page that blocked users see.

stem:
Alpine Ski House wants the Copilot app to be pinned in the second position of the Teams app bar for the sales department. Copilot Chat is allowed for the sales users. The **Pin Copilot Chat** setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center is set to Pin Copilot Chat in Microsoft 365 apps.

What should you do?
choices: Create a Pin Microsoft Copilot Chat cloud policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center for the sales users.
Create a Teams app permission policy that allows the Copilot app for the sales users.
