Create a Teams app setup policy that pins the Copilot app in the second position, and assign it to the sales users.
Deploy the Copilot app to the sales users from Integrated apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
explanation: Pinning settings for Copilot Chat in Teams can only be changed through the Teams admin center. App setup policies pin apps in a defined position, and app permission policies or app centric management decide whether the app is allowed.
rationale: Incorrect: the Pin Microsoft Copilot Chat cloud policy scopes pinning in Microsoft 365 apps to groups, but Learn states that Teams pinning can be changed only in the Teams admin center, and the cloud policy cannot set a position. Use it to scope pinning in other apps.
Incorrect: Copilot Chat is already allowed for the sales users, and a permission policy only allows or blocks apps; it does not pin them. You need it in addition only when the app is blocked.
Correct: an app setup policy with the Copilot app in its pinned apps pins Copilot Chat in the position the policy defines for assigned users, which meets the second-position requirement.

Incorrect: deploying the Copilot app from Integrated apps makes it available in the Copilot app and Outlook, but it does not set its position in the Teams app bar. Use Integrated apps to manage availability of the Copilot app.

stem:
Lucerne Publishing users in a security group named Archive cannot create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks. Other users can. The Cloud Policy setting **Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks** is Not configured for all users. The Archive users were set up last year so that OneDrive is not created for them.

What should you do so that the Archive users can create Copilot Pages?
choices: Set Enable code previews for AI-generated content in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages to Enabled.
Turn on Loop workspaces for the tenant.
Allow OneDrive creation for the Archive users.
Set Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks to Enabled for the Archive group.
explanation: When the Pages and Notebooks policy is Not configured, creation is available. However, if OneDrive creation is disabled for users, they cannot create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks regardless of the policy.
rationale: Incorrect: the code previews policy controls whether users can view and interact with AI-generated code previews, such as lightweight apps. It does not affect whether users can create pages. Use it to allow or block code previews.

Incorrect: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks are independent of Loop and can be enabled even when Loop is blocked, and other users already create pages, so Loop workspaces are not the gap. Turn on Loop when users must work in Loop workspaces.

Correct: Learn notes that users for whom OneDrive creation is disabled cannot create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks, regardless of the policy. Allowing OneDrive creation removes the blocker for the Archive users.

Incorrect: Not configured already makes Pages and Notebooks available, the same as Enabled, so this changes nothing while OneDrive creation stays disabled. Use Enabled or Disabled when you need an explicit setting for a group.

stem:
Northwind Traders wants users without Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses to lose access to Copilot Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app, Outlook, and Teams. Users with Copilot licenses must keep full access. A security group named CopilotLicensed contains all licensed users.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
choices: In Integrated apps, block the Copilot app for the tenant.
In Integrated apps, set the Copilot app so that only CopilotLicensed can install it, and do not deploy it to unlicensed users.
In Integrated apps, turn off the Let users access Microsoft apps in your tenant setting.
Set the Pin Copilot Chat setting to Do not pin Copilot Chat in Microsoft 365 apps and take no other action.
In the Teams admin center, allow the Copilot app only for CopilotLicensed by using app permission policies, and do not pin it for unlicensed users.
explanation: To remove Copilot Chat only for unlicensed users, manage the Copilot app through Integrated apps for the Copilot app and Outlook, and through Teams app permission and setup policies for Teams. Blocking the app in Integrated apps is tenant-wide, and unpinning alone leaves web access.
rationale: Incorrect: blocking the Copilot app through the Integrated apps control blocks it tenant-wide across the Copilot app, Outlook, and the web, including for licensed users. Use it when no one may use Copilot Chat.

Correct: the Copilot app provides Copilot Chat in the Copilot app, Outlook, and on the web. Making it installable only by a group of licensed users, and not deploying it to others, removes it for unlicensed users while licensed users keep it.

Incorrect: Learn states that turning off Let users access Microsoft apps in your tenant does not turn off the Copilot app. You must manage the Copilot app directly. Use that setting to control other Microsoft apps.

Incorrect: the pinning setting only changes the default entry point in the navigation of Microsoft 365 apps. Users can still open Copilot Chat from m365.cloud.microsoft/chat, so it does not remove access. Combine pinning changes with app availability controls when access must be removed.

Correct: Copilot Chat in Teams is managed through the Copilot app in the Teams admin center. Allowing it only for licensed users and not pinning it for others in app setup policies completes the removal in Teams.

stem:
Humongous Insurance must prevent users from sharing their screen or camera with Microsoft 365 Copilot. Claims adjusters must still be able to have voice conversations with Copilot on their mobile devices. Other Copilot features must not change.

What should you do?
choices: Turn off the Screen and camera sharing setting in Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions.
Set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled.
Turn off the Copilot image generation setting in Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions.
Set the EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext policy to block page context.
explanation: Screen and camera sharing manages Vision in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Learn notes that turning it off does not turn off voice, so the setting meets a requirement to block Vision and keep voice conversations.
rationale: Correct: this Copilot actions setting manages Vision, which is how Copilot sees a screen or camera feed, and turning it off does not turn off voice. Claims adjusters keep voice conversations and nothing else changes.

Incorrect: disabling optional connected experiences restricts Copilot Chat, Copilot, and multiple Microsoft 365 experiences, which breaks the requirement that other features stay the same. Use it only to block all optional connected experiences.
Incorrect: image generation controls whether Copilot can create images. It does not stop users from sharing a screen or camera feed. Use it when generated images must be blocked.

Incorrect: EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext stops Copilot Chat in Edge from using web page or PDF content. It does not affect camera or screen sharing in the Copilot app. Use it to keep browser content out of prompts.

stem:
Adventure Works Cycles finds that some employees sign in to the Microsoft Copilot app on corporate devices by using personal Microsoft accounts. The company must stop personal account sign-in to Microsoft services on corporate networks. Work and school accounts must keep using Copilot Chat with enterprise data protection.

What should you do?
choices: Configure tenant restrictions v2 to block Microsoft account tenants.
Block copilot.cloud.microsoft on the corporate proxy.
Set the CopilotPageContext policy in Microsoft Edge to block page context.
Block the Copilot app for all users in Integrated apps.
explanation: Users can sign in to the Copilot app with a work or school account or a personal Microsoft account, and the experiences stay separate. To manage whether users can sign in with personal accounts, Learn points to tenant restrictions v2 as the targeted control.
rationale: Correct: tenant restrictions v2 can block consumer Microsoft account tenants on corporate networks and devices, while work and school sign-ins continue to work with enterprise data protection.
Incorrect: blocking copilot.cloud.microsoft breaks the Copilot app for work accounts too, which the requirements forbid. Learn recommends tenant restrictions instead of blocking this domain.

Incorrect: CopilotPageContext only stops the personal Copilot experience in the Edge work profile from using page or PDF content. It does not block personal sign-in. Use it to keep browser content out of personal Copilot.

Incorrect: blocking the Copilot app in Integrated apps removes Copilot Chat for work accounts across the tenant and does not stop personal accounts from signing in. Use it when no one in the organization may use Copilot Chat.

stem:
Litware, Inc. manages Copilot Chat in the Microsoft Edge sidebar by using Group Policy. You have the following requirements:

- Copilot Chat in Edge for users signed in with their Microsoft Entra account must not use web page or PDF content in responses.
- When users sign in with a personal Microsoft account in the Edge work profile, the personal Copilot experience must not use web page or PDF content either.
- Other Edge sidebar apps must stay available.

Which policy should you configure for each requirement? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

```text
Entra account requirement:            [[1]]
Personal account requirement:         [[2]]
```

targets.label: Box 1
why: Correct: EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext allows or blocks Copilot Chat in Edge from using browsing context, such as web pages and PDFs, for users signed in with Microsoft Entra accounts.

Incorrect: CopilotPageContext applies to the personal Copilot experience when users are signed in with a personal Microsoft account in the work profile. It does not cover Entra-signed-in Copilot Chat.

Incorrect: HubsSidebarEnabled disables Copilot Chat in Edge entirely and blocks all sidebar apps, which breaks the requirement to keep other sidebar apps. Use it when the whole sidebar must be removed.

targets.label: Box 2
why: Incorrect: EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext controls only the Copilot Chat experience for Entra-signed-in users. Personal account usage in the work profile needs its own policy.
Correct: CopilotPageContext prevents Microsoft Copilot for personal use from using web page or PDF content when users are signed in with a personal Microsoft account in the Edge work profile.
Incorrect: HubsSidebarEnabled removes the sidebar and every sidebar app instead of only blocking page content, which breaks the third requirement. Use it to remove the Edge sidebar completely.

explanation: Edge has separate policies for page context: EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext for Copilot Chat with an Entra account, and CopilotPageContext for personal Copilot in the work profile. HubsSidebarEnabled turns off the whole sidebar, including Copilot Chat.

stem:
Contoso, Ltd. enabled usage-based billing for AI experiences in Microsoft 365. Members of a security group named Analysts must be able to use Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork, which is generally available.

What should you do?
choices: Turn on the discovery setting for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.
Allow Analysts on the Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents.
Enroll Analysts in Copilot Frontier.
Create a spending policy that is scoped to Analysts and selects Cowork.
explanation: At general availability, access to Cowork is granted only by a spending policy that includes the user and selects Cowork as a service. The agent entry, the discovery setting, and Frontier do not grant access.
rationale: Incorrect: the discovery setting controls whether users can see Cowork across Microsoft 365, not whether they can use it. When Cowork is discoverable but no billing is set up, users can only request access in the app. Use it to make Cowork visible.

Incorrect: the agent-based control was used in the Frontier and preview versions. The Cowork entry is still visible under All Agents, but configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork. Use it only to view the entry.
Incorrect: Frontier gives preview features before general availability. Cowork is generally available, and its preview access control is deprecated. Use Frontier to evaluate pre-GA features.

Correct: a user can use Cowork when a spending policy in Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration includes the user, directly or through a security group, and selects Cowork under Select agents and services.

stem:
Alpine Ski House has three spending policies that select Cowork. User3 is in the scope of two of them through group membership. User3 moved to a role that must not use Cowork, but must keep the other Copilot experiences.

What should you do?
choices: Remove User3 from the scope of every spending policy that selects Cowork.
Turn off the discovery setting for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.
Turn off the Anthropic model family in Copilot settings.
Lower the per-user limit of both policies to one Copilot credit.
explanation: A spending policy is an access control, not only a budget. Access to Cowork is granted if any applicable policy selects Cowork, so you remove the user from every such policy. A low limit, model settings, and the discovery setting do not remove access.
rationale: Correct: access is decided by whether any applicable policy selects Cowork, so User3 keeps access while any policy that selects Cowork includes User3. Removing User3 from every such scope removes access without affecting other experiences.

Incorrect: the discovery setting controls visibility only, and users covered by a spending policy that selects Cowork have access even when discovery is off. Use the discovery setting to control whether Cowork is shown to users.

Incorrect: model settings control which models appear in the picker, not whether a user can use Cowork, so User3 would keep using Cowork with the other models. Turn off a model family when its terms or data processing are not approved.

Incorrect: Learn states that a low credit limit does not block access; even a one-credit limit still grants it, and enforcement is asynchronous. Lower limits when you want to control spending, not access.

stem:
Fabrikam, Inc. uses Copilot Cowork. The security team must prevent Cowork from completing web tasks for users in Microsoft Edge on their devices. Users must keep their access to Cowork for other tasks.

What should you do?
choices: Remove the users from the spending policies that select Cowork.
Set the HubsSidebarEnabled policy in Microsoft Edge to Disabled.
Set the Allow web search in Copilot policy to Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat.
Turn off the Cowork Browsing tenant setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
explanation: Cowork can complete web tasks in Edge on the user's device by using the user's sign-ins. The Cowork Browsing tenant setting turns this browser use on or off, and existing Edge allow lists, block lists, and view-only policies still apply when it is on.
rationale: Incorrect: removing users from every spending policy that selects Cowork removes Cowork access completely, which breaks the requirement to keep access for other tasks. Do it when users must not use Cowork at all.

Incorrect: HubsSidebarEnabled disables Copilot Chat in Edge and all Edge sidebar apps. It is not the documented control for Cowork browser tasks and affects other sidebar apps. Use it to remove the Edge sidebar.

Incorrect: this web search option stops Cowork from sending web search queries, but browser use is a separate capability that runs tasks in Edge on the device. Use the policy to control web search grounding.
Correct: the Cowork Browsing tenant setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center turns browser use on or off for the organization, so Cowork stops completing web tasks while users keep access to Cowork.

stem:
Woodgrove Bank wants to make a plugin from the Microsoft 365 App Store available in Copilot Cowork. Members of the Finance group must get the plugin automatically and must not be able to remove it. Users outside Finance must not see the plugin.

How should you deploy the plugin?
choices: Make the plugin available in the App Store so that Finance users acquire it.
Deploy the plugin to the entire organization.
Deploy the plugin to specific groups, and select only the Finance group.
Set the plugin to Available to specific users or groups, and select Finance.
explanation: Cowork plugins can be deployed to the entire organization, deployed to specific groups, or made available in the App Store. Deployed plugins are acquired automatically and show Managed by your organization; users can disable but not remove them.
rationale: Incorrect: with App Store availability, users acquire the plugin themselves and can remove it, so Finance would not get it automatically. Use it when users should opt in.
Incorrect: deploying to the entire organization gives the plugin to all licensed Copilot users automatically, so users outside Finance would see it. Use it when every user must have the plugin.

Correct: deploying to specific groups means target users acquire the plugin automatically and cannot remove it, and it is visible to others only if you configure that. This meets all three requirements for Finance.

Incorrect: this availability setting limits who can view the plugin, but users still acquire it themselves, so Finance would not receive it automatically. Use it to restrict an optional plugin to a group.

stem:
Nod Publishers managed access to Copilot Cowork during the preview by allowing a list of users on the Cowork agent entry. Cowork is now generally available, and usage-based billing is enabled. You need the same users, and only those users, to keep access to Cowork.

Which five actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: Add the users from the previous allow list to a security group in Microsoft Entra ID.
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration, and select + Add spending policy.
On the Scope user and group step, choose Specific groups, and select the security group.
On the Select agents and services step, select Cowork.
Set the limits, choose a billing method, and create the policy.
Allow the security group on the Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents.
Enroll the security group in Copilot Frontier.
explanation: At general availability, the agent-based allow list no longer controls Cowork access. You re-express the old allow list as a security group and a spending policy that is scoped to that group and selects Cowork.
rationale: Step 1: the spending policy scopes users through security groups, so the previous allow list must first exist as a Microsoft Entra security group.
Step 2: spending policies are created in Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration by selecting + Add spending policy, which starts the policy wizard.
Step 3: on the Scope user and group step, Specific groups with the new security group limits the policy to the former allow list instead of All users.
Step 4: selecting Cowork under Select agents and services is what grants access; a policy that does not select Cowork gives no Cowork access.
Step 5: setting limits and a billing method and creating the policy completes it, and users in the group's scope then have access to Cowork.
Incorrect: the agent-based access control from the preview is deprecated, and configuration on the All Agents entry has no effect on who can use Cowork. It is the control you are migrating away from.
Incorrect: Frontier gives access to pre-GA features. Cowork is generally available, so Frontier enrollment does not grant or limit Cowork access. Use Frontier for previews.

stem:
Coho Winery uses usage-based billing for Copilot Cowork. A spending policy named Policy1 is scoped to a group named Sales, selects Cowork, and has a per-user limit of one Copilot credit. User1 is a member of Sales. An admin turned off the Anthropic model family in Copilot settings and turned off the discovery setting for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
choices: User1 can use Cowork.
Turning off the discovery setting removes Cowork access for User1.
Because the Anthropic model family is turned off, User1 cannot open Cowork.
explanation: Access to Cowork comes from being in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork, whatever the credit limit. The discovery setting controls visibility, and model settings control which models appear, not access.
rationale: Yes: Policy1 includes User1 through Sales and selects Cowork. A one-credit limit still grants access; limits are a spending safeguard enforced asynchronously, not an access gate.
No: the discovery setting controls visibility only. Usage-based billing setup overrides discovery for users covered by a policy, so User1 keeps access even when discovery is off.

No: turning off the Anthropic family changes which models appear in the model picker. User1 keeps working with the other allowed models, such as GPT models, and Auto selects from the remaining models.

stem:
You need to meet the business requirement for Copilot Cowork access during the pilot.

What should you do?
choices: Turn off the discovery setting for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.
Lower the per-user limit of the Org budget policy to the minimum value.
Block the Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents for all users except AIPilot.
Remove Cowork from the selected services of the Org budget policy.
explanation: Cowork access is granted per service when any applicable spending policy selects Cowork. Because the Org budget policy is scoped to All users and selects Cowork, every user has access until Cowork is removed from that policy.
rationale: Incorrect: the discovery setting controls visibility only, and users covered by a spending policy that selects Cowork have access even when discovery is off. Use it to decide whether Cowork is shown to users.

Incorrect: the one-credit limit already shows the problem: a low limit does not block access, and enforcement is asynchronous. Lowering it further still grants Cowork to everyone. Adjust limits to control spending, not access.
Incorrect: at general availability the Cowork agent entry is still visible, but configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork. Access is granted only through spending policies.

Correct: the Org budget policy covers All users and selects Cowork, which grants Cowork to the whole tenant. Removing Cowork from it leaves the Pilot policy as the only grant, so only AIPilot keeps access while Copilot Chat stays in both policies.

stem:
Tailspin Toys has a Microsoft 365 tenant in the United States commercial cloud. Users see Claude models from Anthropic in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Researcher. The legal team requires that no user can use Claude models until it reviews the terms.

What should you do in the Microsoft 365 admin center?
choices: Set the Allow web search in Copilot policy to Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat.
Disable Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor in the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors setting.
Turn off Anthropic in the AI providers operating as independent processors setting.
Block the Anthropic agents in Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
explanation: Claude models are on by default for most commercial cloud tenants outside the EU, EFTA, and UK, with Anthropic acting as a Microsoft subprocessor. You opt out by disabling Anthropic in the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors setting.
rationale: Incorrect: web search controls whether Copilot grounds answers in Bing results. It has no effect on which AI models are available. Use it when public web content must not be used.

Correct: in regions where Anthropic as a subprocessor is on by default, you select Disable Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor. After that, users no longer have the option to use Claude models, and you can enable them later.

Incorrect: the independent processor setting covers providers that process data under their own terms, such as Anthropic models with Data Retention, which are off by default. The Claude models users see now run as subprocessor models.

Incorrect: agent and plugin access controls which agents users can install or use. Claude models are model choices inside Copilot experiences, not agents. Use agent access settings to block specific agent types.

stem:
Fourth Coffee enabled Anthropic in the **AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors** setting for all users. Users can select Claude in Researcher. Makers report that they cannot select a Claude model for generative responses when they build agents in Copilot Studio.

What should you do?
choices: Enable Anthropic in the AI providers operating as independent processors setting.
Assign the makers to the Copilot Frontier program.
Enable Anthropic models with Data Retention for the makers.
Allow external large language models for generative responses in the Power Platform admin center.
explanation: After Anthropic is enabled in the Microsoft 365 admin center, additional admin controls in the Power Platform admin center decide whether Anthropic can be used in Copilot Studio and Power Platform.
rationale: Incorrect: the independent processor setting is for providers that process data under their own terms. Claude models in Copilot Studio are offered with Anthropic as a subprocessor, so this does not unlock them for makers. Use it only when you accept a provider's own terms.
Incorrect: Frontier gives preview Microsoft 365 features before general availability. It does not control model access in Copilot Studio environments. Use it to evaluate pre-GA features.

Incorrect: Anthropic models with Data Retention are advanced models under Anthropic's own terms that are off by default. Enabling them does not turn on the Power Platform control that makers need. Use them only when the organization accepts data retention by Anthropic.

Correct: Learn states that once Anthropic is enabled in the Microsoft 365 admin center, additional controls in the Power Platform admin center allow it in Copilot Studio and Power Platform, through the setting to allow external LLMs for generative responses.

stem:
Trey Research has Claude models enabled for all users with Anthropic as a Microsoft subprocessor. The research group wants to use an Anthropic model that is labeled as an Anthropic model with Data Retention. The legal team accepts that Anthropic stores inputs and outputs under its own commercial terms. Other users must not be able to use this model.

What should you do?
choices: Take no action, because the model is available to every user who can use Claude models as a subprocessor.
Allow the use of preview models for the research group in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Scope the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors setting to the research group only.
Opt in to Anthropic models with Data Retention, accept the Anthropic terms, and select the research group as the users who can access them.
explanation: Anthropic models with Data Retention are off by default even where other Claude models are on. Using them requires an explicit opt-in under Anthropic's Commercial Terms and Data Protection Addendum, with Anthropic acting as an independent processor, and the admin chooses which users or groups can access them.
rationale: Incorrect: Learn states that Anthropic models with Data Retention must always be separately enabled, even where other Claude models are on by default. They are not covered by the subprocessor setting.

Incorrect: preview models are the latest models offered for exploration and testing, not recommended for production. Allowing them is a separate control and does not accept Anthropic's data retention terms. Use it when users must test new preview models.

Incorrect: scoping the subprocessor setting only changes who can use the subprocessor Claude models, and it would take them away from other users. It does not enable models with Data Retention. Use it to limit standard Claude models to a group.

Correct: no users have access to these models until the tenant admin explicitly opts in, accepts Anthropic's terms, and chooses all users or specific users or groups, so selecting only the research group meets both requirements.

stem:
Contoso Pharmaceuticals has a Microsoft 365 tenant in the European Union that existed before March 2026. All users must be able to use Claude models in Copilot experiences in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Claude models must not be available in the Microsoft Copilot app, Researcher, or Copilot Studio.

Which option should you select under **Choose which users can access Anthropic models**?
choices: Specific users and groups, with a group that contains all users
All users for Microsoft 365 apps only
No users
All users
explanation: For tenants in the EU, EFTA, and UK, the Anthropic subprocessor setting has an option that makes Claude models available only in Copilot experiences in Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. It is on by default only for tenants created after March 25, 2026, so older tenants must check it.
rationale: Incorrect: a group that contains everyone has the same effect as All users, because the assignment applies across Copilot and Copilot Studio experiences. Use specific groups when only some users may use Claude.

Correct: All users for Microsoft 365 apps only makes Claude models available only in Copilot experiences in Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, which keeps them out of the Copilot app, Researcher, and Copilot Studio.
Incorrect: No users is the default for EU tenants created before March 25, 2026, and it blocks Claude models in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint too. Keep it when Claude must not be used at all.

Incorrect: All users makes Claude models available beyond Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps, including experiences such as the Copilot app and Researcher, which the requirement forbids. Use it when Claude may be used everywhere.

stem:
Litware, Inc. is documenting how each AI model used in its Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences is classified, because the classification decides which contractual terms apply.

Which classification should you assign to each model? To answer, drag the appropriate classifications to the correct models. Each classification may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
choices: AI model hosted and operated by Microsoft
AI subprocessor
AI independent processor
Preview model
targets: Model1: an Azure OpenAI model hosted on Azure
Model2: a Claude model offered under the Microsoft Product Terms and DPA
Model3: an Anthropic model with Data Retention used under the Anthropic Commercial Terms
Model4: a Black Forest Labs FLUX model hosted on Azure
explanation: Microsoft classifies AI functionality by who processes data: Microsoft-hosted models and AI subprocessors are covered by the Microsoft DPA and Product Terms, while AI independent processors use their own terms and are off unless an admin enables them.
rationale: Model1: Azure OpenAI is hosted on Azure and provided directly by Microsoft under the DPA and Product Terms, and the data does not leave Microsoft.
Model2: Anthropic handles data on Microsoft's behalf under the Microsoft DPA, Product Terms, and enterprise safeguards, which is the definition of an AI subprocessor.
Model3: for Anthropic models with Data Retention, Anthropic processes data under its own commercial terms and data processing agreement, which makes it an AI independent processor.
Model4: Learn lists Black Forest Labs FLUX as an example of a model hosted on Azure and provided directly by Microsoft, so it is a Microsoft-hosted model like Azure OpenAI.
notes: AI model hosted and operated by Microsoft: a model hosted on Azure and provided by Microsoft, such as Azure OpenAI or FLUX. Covered by the DPA and Product Terms; data does not leave Microsoft.

AI subprocessor: a third-party provider that processes data on Microsoft's behalf under the Microsoft DPA and Product Terms, such as Anthropic for standard Claude models. Managed in the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors setting.
AI independent processor: a third-party provider that processes data under its own commitments and terms, outside the Microsoft DPA. Not used unless an admin enables it.

Preview model: a newly available model for exploration and testing that is not recommended for production. It describes release status, not who processes the data, so it does not fit these contractual classifications.

stem:
Lucerne Publishing has a Microsoft 365 tenant in the European Union, so Claude models are set to No users by default. Members of a group named Makers must build agents in Copilot Studio that use a Claude model for generative responses. You are an AI Administrator.

Which five actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Settings > View all, and select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors.
Under Available subprocessors for your organization, select Anthropic, and then select Save.
Under the setting for who can access Anthropic models, select the Makers group, and then select Save.
In the Power Platform admin center, allow external large language models for generative responses in the environment that Makers use.
In Copilot Studio, select a Claude model during agent creation.
Select AI providers operating as independent processors, and turn on Anthropic.
Under the setting for who can access Anthropic models, select All users for Microsoft 365 apps only.
explanation: In opt-in regions, you first enable Anthropic as a subprocessor and choose who can access it in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Only then do the additional Power Platform admin center controls let Copilot Studio use it, and makers select the model when they create an agent.
rationale: Step 1: the opt-in starts on the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors page, which you reach from Copilot > Settings > View all as an AI Administrator or Global Administrator.
Step 2: selecting Anthropic under Available subprocessors for your organization and saving turns on Anthropic as a subprocessor for the tenant.
Step 3: choosing the Makers group limits access to the provider. Assignments apply at the provider level across Copilot and Copilot Studio experiences.

Step 4: Learn states that once Anthropic is enabled in the Microsoft 365 admin center, additional controls in the Power Platform admin center allow it in Copilot Studio, so this step must come after the opt-in.
Step 5: in Copilot Studio, creators must select the model during agent creation, which is possible only after both admin controls allow it.

Incorrect: the independent processor setting is for providers that use their own terms, such as Anthropic models with Data Retention. Standard Claude models for Copilot Studio are enabled through the subprocessor setting.

Incorrect: this option makes Claude models available only in Copilot experiences in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, so Makers could not use them in Copilot Studio. Use it when Claude is allowed only in those apps.

stem:
You need to configure access to Claude models to meet the business requirements of Relecloud.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
choices: On the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors page, select Anthropic under Available subprocessors for your organization, and save.
Under the setting for who can access Anthropic models, select specific users and groups, and add AIPilot.
Under the setting for who can access Anthropic models, select All users for Microsoft 365 apps only.
Opt in to Anthropic models with Data Retention for AIPilot.
In the Power Platform admin center, allow external large language models for generative responses.
explanation: The Relecloud tenant is in the EU Data Boundary, where Claude models are set to No users by default. You opt in to Anthropic as a subprocessor and scope access to AIPilot, which keeps processing under the Microsoft Product Terms and DPA.
rationale: Correct: in EU tenants, Anthropic as a subprocessor defaults to No users, so you must select Anthropic and save. As a subprocessor, Anthropic is covered by the Microsoft Product Terms and DPA, which the business requirements demand.
Correct: scoping access to AIPilot gives the pilot users Claude models across Copilot experiences, including the Copilot app and Researcher, while other users stay without access.

Incorrect: this option limits Claude models to Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, so AIPilot could not use them in the Copilot app or Researcher. Use it when Claude is allowed only inside those apps.

Incorrect: Anthropic models with Data Retention are used under Anthropic's own terms, with Anthropic as an independent processor, so they are not covered by the Microsoft DPA. Use them only when the legal team accepts Anthropic's retention terms.
Incorrect: the Power Platform admin center control allows Anthropic in Copilot Studio and Power Platform. Relecloud needs Claude in the Copilot app and Researcher, not in Copilot Studio agents.

stem:
Graphic Design Institute uses Copilot Cowork. The data protection officer requires that Cowork no longer uses Claude models from Anthropic. Users with Cowork access must keep using Cowork with other models.

What should you do?
choices: Turn off the discovery setting for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.
Turn off the Anthropic model family in Copilot settings.
Turn off the Cowork Browsing tenant setting.
Remove the users from every spending policy that selects Cowork.
explanation: Model settings control which models users see, not whether they can use Cowork. When the Anthropic family is off, users with Cowork access keep working with the other allowed models, such as GPT models, and Auto picks from the remaining models.
rationale: Incorrect: the discovery setting controls whether users can see Cowork across Microsoft 365. It does not affect model choice. Use it to manage the visibility of usage-billed experiences.
Correct: turning off the Anthropic model family in Copilot settings removes Claude models from the picker, and users keep Cowork access with the remaining models, which meets both requirements.
Incorrect: Cowork Browsing controls whether Cowork can complete web tasks in Microsoft Edge on the user's device. It does not affect which models Cowork uses. Turn it off to stop browser tasks.
Incorrect: spending policies grant access to Cowork, so removing users from them takes Cowork away completely. Do this when users must not use Cowork at all.

stem:
Wide World Importers wants Microsoft 365 Copilot to use knowledge articles from its ServiceNow instance. You are an AI Administrator and plan to use a prebuilt synced Copilot connector.

Which page in the Microsoft 365 admin center should you use to start the deployment?
choices: Copilot > Connectors > Gallery
Agents > Tools
Settings > Integrated apps
Copilot > Search > Bookmarks
explanation: Synced Copilot connectors are deployed from Copilot > Connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center. On the Gallery, you select the data source, name the connection, enter the URL, choose authentication, and optionally stage the rollout to a subset of users.
rationale: Correct: Learn tells you to choose Copilot > Connectors, select Gallery, and pick the data source, such as ServiceNow Knowledge, to create the connection.
Incorrect: Agents > Tools manages plugins and tools, such as plugins for Cowork, including who can use them. It is not where connector connections are created. Use it to allow or block plugins.
Incorrect: Integrated apps deploys and blocks apps and agents, including the Copilot app. It does not create Copilot connector connections. Use it to manage app availability.
Incorrect: Bookmarks promote individual URLs for keywords in Copilot Search. They do not index content from ServiceNow. Use them for a small set of key resources.

stem:
Woodgrove Bank wants Microsoft 365 Copilot to answer questions by using data from an external system that contains regulated, frequently changing records. The data must stay in the source system and must not be indexed in Microsoft 365. Each user must access the data with their own credentials.

Which type of Copilot connector should you use?
choices: a custom synced connector built by using the Microsoft Graph connectors API
a synced connector with tenant configuration
a federated connector
a synced connector with self-serve configuration
explanation: Synced connectors crawl and index external content into Microsoft Graph. Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time with the user's identity, without indexing it, which suits sensitive, dynamic, or live data.
rationale: Incorrect: a custom connector built with the Microsoft Graph connectors API is a synced connector that ingests items into the Microsoft Graph index, which breaks the requirement that data stays in the source. Use one to index a line-of-business system that has no prebuilt connector.

Incorrect: a synced connector with tenant configuration indexes data into Microsoft Graph at the organization level, which breaks the requirement that data stays in the source. Use it for broad indexing of knowledge repositories.
Correct: federated connectors fetch data live through MCP, keep data in the source system, and use user-level authentication, which matches regulated, changing data that must not be indexed.
Incorrect: self-serve synced connectors use the user's own credentials, but they still index the user's content into Microsoft Graph. Use them to index personally relevant content.

stem:
Northwind Traders is deploying a synced Copilot connector for a public product knowledge base. Most employees do not have accounts in the knowledge base system, but every employee must be able to find all articles through Copilot.

Which setting should you configure on the **Users** tab of the custom setup?
choices: Deploy the connector to a subset of users for validation.
Set Access Permissions to Only users with access to the content.
Provide a custom mapping formula in Map Identities.
Set Access Permissions to Everyone in the organization.
explanation: On the Users tab of a synced connector, Access Permissions decide whether indexed data is visible only to users with access in the source or to everyone in the organization. Identity mapping matters only when source permissions are enforced.
rationale: Incorrect: deploying to a subset of users is a staged rollout for validation before broad deployment. It limits who sees the content rather than opening it to everyone. Use it for a pilot.
Incorrect: this option enforces source permissions, so employees without accounts in the knowledge base would see nothing. Use it when the source system restricts content to specific users.

Incorrect: Map Identities changes how source users are matched to Microsoft Entra users, by default by email to UserPrincipalName or Mail. It cannot grant access to employees who have no source account. Use it when emails do not match.
Correct: Everyone in the organization makes the indexed articles visible to all employees, even those without accounts in the source system, which fits public content.

stem:
Fabrikam, Inc. uses a synced Copilot connector with incremental crawls every 15 minutes and a full crawl once a month. After the source system administrators removed a team's access to several items, members of that team still see those items in Copilot responses two weeks later.

What should you do?
choices: Schedule full crawls more often so that permission changes are processed.
Change the content property of the connection.
Assign the title semantic label to a different property.
Increase the incremental crawl frequency to the shortest interval.
explanation: Incremental crawls process only new or changed items and do not process permission updates. Full crawls update ACLs, detect deletions, and apply schema changes, so you run them periodically to keep permissions accurate.
rationale: Correct: Learn states that incremental crawls do not support permission updates and that you should run full crawls periodically. A more frequent full crawl applies the removed access sooner.
Incorrect: the content property drives full-text indexing, snippets, and ranking. It has nothing to do with access control lists. Change it when search relevance or snippets are poor.
Incorrect: the title semantic label decides which property is shown as the item title and enables result clusters. It does not affect permissions. Remap it when titles appear wrong.

Incorrect: 15 minutes is already the shortest interval, and incremental crawls never process permission changes, however often they run. Use frequent incremental crawls to keep content and metadata fresh.

stem:
Adventure Works Cycles deploys a synced Copilot connector to a SaaS data source in North America. The connection fails to crawl because the data source accepts traffic only from approved IP addresses. Users already reach Copilot without network issues.

What should you do?
choices: Switch the connection from full crawls to incremental crawls only.
Change the connector authentication method to a service account with more permissions.
Allow the Copilot connector service IP ranges for the region in the data source firewall.
Allow the entire *.cloud.microsoft domain on the corporate proxy.
explanation: If a data source uses IP firewall rules, you must allow the Copilot connectors service IP ranges, which Microsoft publishes per region for Microsoft 365 Enterprise and Government, so the service can crawl the source.
rationale: Incorrect: the crawl type does not change the source IP addresses of the connector service, so incremental crawls would fail in the same way and would also skip permission updates. Tune crawl types for freshness, not connectivity.
Incorrect: more permissions do not help when the firewall drops the connection before authentication. Check the service account roles when the crawl connects but cannot read content.
Correct: the crawler connects from the Copilot connectors service, so the data source firewall must allow the published IP ranges for the NAM region, such as 52.250.92.252/30 and 52.224.250.216/30.

Incorrect: *.cloud.microsoft must be allowed for users to reach Copilot, but users already connect, and the blocked traffic is inbound to the data source from the connector service. Allow the domain when clients cannot reach Copilot.

stem:
Proseware, Inc. uses a ServiceNow Knowledge Copilot connector connection that was published six months ago. Copilot answers link to the default ServiceNow article URL, but the company publishes articles on a custom portal URL. You need Copilot responses to use the custom portal URL by setting a new default expression for the URL property.

What should you do?
choices: Edit the existing connection, and change the default expression for the URL property on the Content tab.
Add an alias for the URL property on the existing connection.
Create a new connection with Custom setup, and set the default expression for the URL property on the Content tab before you publish.
Add a bookmark for the custom portal URL in Copilot Search.
explanation: Some connectors, such as ServiceNow, let you customize schema property values such as the access URL with a default expression. This is done during connection setup; editing an existing connection to change schema property values is not supported.
rationale: Incorrect: editing an existing connection to change schema property values is not currently supported, so the URL of the published connection cannot be changed this way. Edit an existing connection for supported changes, such as the crawl schedule.

Incorrect: aliases are friendly names that normalize property names across connections for queries and filters. They do not change the value that the URL property returns. Use aliases to build one filter across several connections.

Correct: Learn states that to customize schema property values you must create a new connection, select Custom setup, and set the new default expression in Manage properties on the Content tab before publishing.
Incorrect: a bookmark promotes one URL for selected keywords in search. It does not change the links in Copilot responses for indexed articles. Use bookmarks to surface key sites.

targets.label: Box 1
why: Correct: the title semantic label marks the property shown as the item title in search and other Microsoft 365 experiences, and it is the most important label for result clusters.
Incorrect: the url label marks the target URL of the item in the source system. A ticket title is not a URL. Map it to the property that holds the link to the ticket.
Incorrect: the fileName label marks the name of a file. Tickets are not files. Use it for connectors that index documents.

targets.label: Box 2
why: Correct: a queryable property supports property-specific queries by name, such as priority:High, which is the requirement.
Incorrect: a searchable property adds its text to the full-text index so a free-text query matches it, but it does not enable name-specific queries. Use it for text such as titles and descriptions.

Incorrect: a refinable property can be used as a filter on the search results page, and the refinable attribute cannot be changed after setup. It does not by itself support priority:High queries. Use it to build filters.

targets.label: Box 3
why: Correct: Update-MgExternalConnectionSchema creates or updates the schema of an existing connection, which matches the hash table that defines baseType and properties.

Incorrect: New-MgExternalConnection creates the connection itself with an ID, name, and description. The connection already exists, and this body is a schema. Use it as the first step of a custom connector.
Incorrect: Set-MgExternalConnectionItem ingests one external item with its ACL, properties, and content after the schema exists. Use it to push tickets into the index.

explanation: A custom synced connector is built in three stages: create the connection, register the schema with properties, attributes, and semantic labels, and then ingest items with ACLs. Search schema attributes are search, query, retrieve, and refine, and semantic labels such as title connect properties to Microsoft 365 experiences.

stem:
Contoso Suites is building a custom synced Copilot connector for its HR case system by using Microsoft Graph PowerShell with delegated permissions. You must follow the principle of least privilege.

Which four actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy", "ExternalItem.ReadWrite.OwnedBy"`
`New-MgExternalConnection -BodyParameter @{ id = "contosohr"; name = "Contoso HR"; description = "HR cases" }`
`Update-MgExternalConnectionSchema -ExternalConnectionId "contosohr" -BodyParameter $schema`
`Set-MgExternalConnectionItem -ExternalConnectionId "contosohr" -ExternalItemId $itemId -BodyParameter $item`
`Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "SearchConfiguration.ReadWrite.All"`
`New-MgSearchAcronym -BodyParameter $params`
`Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All", "ExternalItem.ReadWrite.All"`
explanation: A custom synced connector uses the Microsoft Graph connectors API: connect with the connection and item permissions, create the connection, register its schema, and then ingest items that carry content, properties, and an ACL.
rationale: Step 1: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy and ExternalItem.ReadWrite.OwnedBy are the least privileged permissions for creating a connection, its schema, and its items.
Step 2: New-MgExternalConnection creates the connection with its ID, name, and description. The schema and items both reference this connection ID.
Step 3: Update-MgExternalConnectionSchema registers the properties, search attributes, and semantic labels. Items must match the schema, so it comes before ingestion.
Step 4: Set-MgExternalConnectionItem ingests each HR case with its ACL, properties, and content into the Microsoft Graph index, where Copilot and search can use it.
Incorrect: SearchConfiguration.ReadWrite.All grants access to search answers such as acronyms and bookmarks, not to connector connections or items. Use it when you manage search answers with Graph.
Incorrect: New-MgSearchAcronym creates an acronym answer for Copilot Search. It does not ingest HR cases. Use it to curate organization-specific acronyms.
Incorrect: the .All permissions work but are higher privileged than the .OwnedBy permissions, which breaks least privilege. Use them only when the app must manage connections it does not own.
